baseline: N4 (decisions-ui-reimplementation-2026-07-26.md) — the SHIPPED-BEHAVIOUR baseline. CORRECTED 2026-08-07: this field previously read 'supersedes Figma; file 5vWxC85QBhqbzPU30RP7LH re-verified 2026-08-06 and holds no product screens'. That is FALSE. The operator showed the file's Pages list: an ELITEA-UI section (Sidebar Menu, Onboarding, Maintenance Page, Import Modal, Announcement Banner, Support ChatBot, Responsive Behavior, Empty State Pages, Modals, Errors, Login, Feedback Popover (NPS), Light Theme screens), plus '*** Colors', '*** Cards redesign guide', '*** Improvements', and AGENT HUB / CHAT / AGENTS sections covering the surfaces being reimplemented. The 'one Cover frame' finding came from a quota-exhausted View-seat inspection that the ADR itself marked 'needs operator confirmation'; that confirmation never happened and the hedge was dropped in transit. These screenshots record what the OLD APP DOES (quirks included); Figma records DESIGN INTENT. They answer different questions and neither supersedes the other.

That withheld state is part of what the baseline pins.

The E2E stack runs the gateway without one, so that banner is the DEFAULT state here rather than an edge case.

The brand-pack editor (ADR-0024 WP4): the grouped form with every field at inherit, the two-scheme preview built from the product default, the derived swatch strips and the Layers panel. The E2E stack mounts no file pack and the branding journey restores the database layer after itself, so the reference is the all-inherit state on purpose.

userPublicHowTo.whatItIs: The author public-library page: everything a given AUTHOR has published. Parity target apps/elitea-ui/src/pages/UserPublic/UserPublic.jsx.
userPublicHowTo.howToReach: Open Agent HUB and click the small round AUTHOR AVATAR at the bottom-left of any agent card (see agents-hub.*.jpeg). Cards with 2 avatars have multiple authors. This is the only in-app entry point.
userPublicHowTo.note: Use an author who has published something — e.g. the author of 'AI Presentation Creator' (85 likes) in Agent HUB. Your own id is 33731, but that library is empty, so it would only show the empty state.
userPublicHowTo.resolved: Captured 2026-08-06. Bare /user-public/ 404s (no :tab). Note the deployed app is version 2.0.4 while the parity baseline apps/elitea-ui is pinned at a55f36cf / 0.4.1863 (2026-07-08) — treat old-SPA route contracts as advisory, not authoritative.

coverage.provenance: 63 shots captured from production (see `source`/`captured`); 12 admin shots added by #229 with no production capture — see `adminSurface`; 3 pipeline-editor STATE shots added with no production capture — see `pipelineEditorSurface`. `shots` read 75 while the array held 76: the `/admin/app/governance` row was appended without it, and the number is now the real count rather than a stale one nothing checks (no gate reads this field — `scripts/check-visual-coverage.mjs` counts the array).

pipelineEditorSurface.what: The pipeline editor's three NEW states, on the route the index already carried two rows for: a canvas authored through the Add-node menu, a node card carrying admission issues, and the interrupt switches disabled with their reason. The two existing rows move from `ready` to `wired` in the same change and are claimed by the same spec.
pipelineEditorSurface.whyTheyAreStates: The index is otherwise one row per ROUTE-and-theme, because a production capture is a screenshot of a URL. These three are not new URLs — they are states of one editor that only exist once a user has acted, and each is a distinct rendering with its own failure mode. Filing them as rows is what makes `scripts/check-visual-coverage.mjs` able to see them at all; the alternative was three baselines with no index row, which is the shape of gap #229 was about.
pipelineEditorSurface.file: null on all three, and on nothing else about them: there is NO production JPEG, because these states postdate the 2026-08-06 capture by two months. `baseline` names the Playwright PNG instead, the way the admin rows do.
pipelineEditorSurface.howTheyAreReached: e2e/visual/pipeline-editor.visual.spec.ts serves the pipeline's OWN application-detail GET from a fixed document and lets every other request reach the real stack. It creates no server row, deliberately: a pipeline alive in the tenant would break `pipelines-list-empty`, which waits for `You have no pipelines.` in a parallel worker of the same run. That file's header states in full what the arrangement does and does not pin.
pipelineEditorSurface.notCaptured: The RUN FEED (`data-performing`, the `Run N details` node) — it needs a live turn, so it needs the runtime plane, the worker and a model backend, none of which the `visual` job's stack has. It is asserted instead, against a real run, by e2e/streaming/chat.pipeline-authored.spec.ts. Also the Yaml tab, the collapsed panels, and the node configuration pickers.

wiringStatusReview.what: wiringStatus was authored in 46a90914 using route-wiring-map.json’s PHASE-0 vocabulary. At that moment 38 route files under src/routes/** rendered RouteShell scaffolding instead of the page components already built for them, and “ready” meant exactly that: the page exists, the ROUTE does not render it. It never meant the UI was a stub.
wiringStatusReview.why: The wiring plan has since run. route-wiring-map.json now reports 50 routes wired and its generator’s own --check passes against the tree, so the map is current and the screenshot index was simply never updated alongside it. Wave 2 then mounted more UI still (#128 chat conversation sidebar, #149 toolkit/MCP Indexes tab, #134/#148 agent version bar).
wiringStatusReview.evidence: Every route flipped below was ALSO opened against the running e2e stack and confirmed to render its real page rather than a heading-only shell, and — except /help-center — put through the stall experiment recorded per-entry in e2e/visual/routes.visual.spec.ts before being given a baseline. No route was flipped merely to make it snapshottable.

notFlipped./onboarding: Renders a real page, but not the screen this index describes (a 48-slide tour). That is a parity question, not a wiring one. Not measured, not flipped.
notFlipped./agents/:tab/:agentId + /pipelines/:tab/: Detail/editor routes needing a seeded entity to reach with real data. Not measured, not flipped.
notFlipped./user-public/*: Needs an author with published content; the seeded tenant has none. needs-route-state is accurate.
notFlipped./chat/:conversationId: Already wired; remains EXEMPT for determinism (a per-run conversation grows the sidebar list).

exemptAfterFlip./help-center: Flipped to wired (the route renders its real page) but EXEMPT from snapshots: useResourcesConfig has no backend (issue #26), so all five cards render “No links configured” and the version bar is blank. A baseline would make a screen with no content the official reference.

adminSurface.what: The ten /admin/app/* routes, derived from src/pages/admin/router.tsx's own route table (src/pages/admin/adminVisualIndex.test.ts asserts the two cannot drift, the way AdminNav.test.tsx does for the nav).
adminSurface.whyTheyWereMissing: This index was captured from next.elitea.ai on 2026-08-06, when /admin/app/ was served by the separate admin_ui SPA and elitea-web's admin entry was a ~160-line placeholder. A parity index of elitea-web reasonably had no admin rows. #200 then ported ten real admin pages into this app and #223 retired the submodule and pinned the published image at target: final (which is FROM e2e), so the admin SPA this bundle builds is the one that ships.
adminSurface.file: null on every admin row, and that is a fact rather than an omission: there is NO production JPEG for these screens. The other 63 rows point at a captured screenshot of the OLD app; the admin rows point at nothing, because the app that served those URLs in production was admin_ui, which no longer exists in this repo. `baseline` names the Playwright PNG instead — that is what these rows are compared against.
adminSurface.humanReference: apps/admin-ui is gone (#223). The read-only reference each ported page names in its own module header is frontends/admin_ui/frontend/src/pages/**, outside this repo.
adminSurface.notCaptured: The admin index route (/admin/app/, which renders AdminUsers rather than redirecting), every dialog and drawer, and the non-default tab of each page. Listed in e2e/visual/admin.visual.spec.ts's NOT COVERED block with the reason for each.
